title: MEXT School Basic Survey: Collegiate Computing and Engineering Admissions, Faculty Demographics, and Gender Parity
source_name: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
description: Longitudinal census tracking undergraduate admissions across engineering and computer science faculties in Japan, analyzing the relational impacts of female faculty representation, interdisciplinary curriculum design, and tech industry internships on female enrollment rates.
observation_unit: Academic discipline panel data across national, public, and private universities in Japan
sample_population_note: Annual School Basic Survey census covering all 800+ universities in Japan
sample_population_size: Complete census of Japanese university admissions
title_ja: 【学校基本調査】大学情報系・理工系学部における女性比率・教員構成・学際カリキュラムの多変量分析

research_angles.title: Institutional Role Models vs Curricular Flexibility: What Really Drives Female Participation in Japanese Collegiate Informatics?
research_questions: Does female faculty representation or interdisciplinary curriculum design more strongly predict female student enrollment in computing?
Are traditional engineering disciplines stalling in gender parity compared to informatics?
hypotheses: Faculty female ratio demonstrates a statistically significant positive predictive relationship with female student enrollment rate.
Interdisciplinary curriculum index exhibits strong independent explanatory power (VIF < 2.0), showing that broadening computing beyond narrow hardware engineering attracts diverse talent.
research_angles.theoretical_framework: Social Cognitive Career Theory (Lent, Brown & Hackett) and Gender Schema Theory
